title: Block Sudo Commands
summary: A Claude Code hook that blocks any Bash command starting with sudo or doas and tells the agent to hand the exact command to you for a manual run.
description: Root access should be a decision you make, not a side effect of a long task. This PreToolUse hook looks at the first word of every command in a chain and refuses sudo and doas, even after env assignments or time and nohup prefixes.
It also catches sudo tucked inside a sh -c string. The message asks the agent to print the command and the reason, so you can run it in your own terminal when it is truly needed.
useWhen: Run an agent on a laptop where sudo has no password prompt
Keep package installs inside the user account
Make elevated steps an explicit human choice
Review system changes before they happen

hook.command: node -e "let d='';process.stdin.on('data',c=>d+=c).on('end',()=>{let j={};try{j=JSON.parse(d)||{}}catch(e){process.exit(0)}const i=j.tool_input||{};const q=String.fromCharCode(34),sq=String.fromCharCode(39),bs=String.fromCharCode(92),nl=String.fromCharCode(10);const c=String(i.command||'');const first=c.split(/[;&|]+/).some(s=>/^[(]?(sudo|doas)([ ]|$)/.test(s.trim().replace(/^([A-Za-z_]+=[^ ]*[ ]+|(time|nohup|exec|env|command|xargs)[ ]+)+/,'')));const nested=/(^|[ ])(a|ba|da|z)?sh[ ]+-c[ ]+.?(sudo|doas)[ ]/.test(c);if(first||nested){console.error('Blocked: sudo needs a person. Print the exact command, say why it needs root, and ask the user to run it in their own terminal.');process.exit(2)}})"

example.prompt: Install the missing library with sudo apt install libpq-dev.
example.result: Blocked. The agent prints the apt command, explains why root is needed and waits for you to run it yourself.

faq.question: Does it stop the word sudo inside a commit message?
faq.answer: No. Only a command that starts with sudo or doas, or a sh -c payload that does, is refused. Text elsewhere on the line is ignored.

faq.question: Can I allow one safe sudo command?
faq.answer: Edit the pattern to skip a command you trust, or run that single command in your own shell as the message suggests.

access: Reads the Bash command text before execution
Refuses commands whose first word is sudo or doas
Executes nothing and writes no files
